featured_videos.title: Why I’m Doing the Lion Diet Instead of Carnivore
featured_videos.creator: Emmathecarnivore
featured_videos.editorial_title: Why I’m Doing the Lion Diet Instead of Carnivore
featured_videos.commentary: Emma's 30-day lion diet update is a great example of why elimination diets work so well for figuring out what your body actually tolerates. Stripping it back to just beef, salt, and water isn't for everyone, but when someone feels noticeably better after a month, that's hard to argue with. If you're curious about the approach, check out our lion diet breakdown for the full story. The top comment on this one nails it: carnivore was always meant to be customizable, and if your version is working, that's all that matters.

featured_videos.title: The "Biological Cost" of Ozempic & Mounjaro
featured_videos.creator: Kent Carnivore
featured_videos.commentary: The comments here are brutal but they're pointing at something real: there's a difference between losing weight and being healthy. People on GLP-1s are shrinking fast, yeah, but the facial wasting, the sunken look, the neurological oddities people are reporting. that's not just weight loss in action. That's metabolic stress. The body's fighting back because you're essentially tricking your brain into ignoring hunger signals instead of fixing what caused the overeating in the first place. I covered how the body adapts to different ways of eating, and GLP-1s skip that entirely. they're a chemical shortcut that ignores the actual problem. The lawsuits are coming because people are realizing the "cost" of rapid weight loss when your body's screaming that something's wrong.

featured_videos.title: 500 Days STALLED on Carnivore & THEN THIS HAPPENED!
featured_videos.creator: HomeSteadHow
featured_videos.editorial_title: 500 Days STALLED on Carnivore & THEN THIS HAPPENED!
featured_videos.commentary: A 500-day stall would break most people. But what gets me about Jen's story is that she didn't quit on carnivore, she quit on *dairy*, and that one shift cracked the code wide open. The comments are full of people saying the same thing, that Kelly Hogan's line about choosing between dairy and weight loss hit different for them too. If you've been stuck, it might not be that carnivore doesn't work for you. it might be that you need to dig into what's actually working against you, and for a lot of women especially, that turns out to be heavy cream and cheese. Check our dairy breakdown if you're wondering whether it's a culprit in your stall.

featured_videos.title: Inside Dr. Ken Berry’s REAL Daily Life | Carnivore, Family & Farm
featured_videos.creator: Courtney Luna
featured_videos.editorial_title: Inside Dr. Ken Berry’s REAL Daily Life | Carnivore, Family & Farm
featured_videos.commentary: People love seeing the person behind the credentials, and this video hits different because it's just two humans talking about what actually works instead of lecturing from a stage. The "rubber band theory" comment got me too, because that's exactly how most people experience their relationship with food, and it's refreshing to hear it named so plainly. What strikes me most is how grounded Dr. Berry's approach is, not just to carnivore but to life, family, and avoiding the noise of modern culture. That kind of clarity matters because it shows this isn't about perfectionism or obsession, it's about actually living better with less inflammation and more peace.

featured_videos.title: New House Life | Costco haul, organizing the kitchen, baby plans, long-term carnivore effects
featured_videos.creator: Steak and Butter Vlogs
featured_videos.editorial_title: New House Life | Costco haul, organizing the kitchen, baby plans, long-term carnivore effects
featured_videos.commentary: This is what carnivore sustainability looks like in real life. Not just the meals or the macros, but someone building a home, planning a future, and making intentional choices about timing and readiness. The comments hit on something important that gets lost in diet debates: what works for you depends on where you actually are in life right now. She's respecting her husband's timeline, he's respecting hers, and they're both thriving on meat while figuring out the bigger picture. That's the stuff that actually matters long-term, way more than any kitchen hack or Costco haul.

featured_videos.title: The 10 Best Countries for Carnivores (Eat Meat in Peace)
featured_videos.creator: Shawn Baker MD
featured_videos.editorial_title: The 10 Best Countries for Carnivores (Eat Meat in Peace)
featured_videos.commentary: The meat culture divide is real, and these comments prove it. You've got Argentines bringing 2,700 kilos of beef to the World Cup, New Zealanders raised on wild game, and Spaniards treating chorizo like art form, while simultaneously fighting Brussels bureaucrats trying to convince them meat causes cancer. What strikes me is that this isn't just about food preference or tradition. These countries have lower rates of the metabolic diseases we see everywhere else, and nobody's arguing about it because nobody's confused about what they're eating. It's worth asking yourself: does your food culture support what your body actually needs, or are you swimming against the current?
